question: Should QQBot expose channel- and account-level `contextVisibility` under the existing shared policy contract once runtime proof confirms that restrictive deployments neither leak unverified quote text nor lose permitted bot quote context?
rationale: This is a security-boundary and operator-facing configuration decision; tests in the PR body do not establish the real QQBot ingress and quote-cache behavior needed to accept the compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Require runtime proof and contract confirmation
options.body: Keep the existing shared policy design, but require redacted evidence for every quote-author path and confirmation that QQBot config precedence matches other channels before merge.

options.title: Narrow to the security fix only
options.body: Avoid adding QQBot-local configuration acceptance if the existing global/default context-visibility setting already provides the required operator control.

recommendation.title: Require runtime proof and contract confirmation
recommendation.body: Keep the existing shared policy design, but require redacted evidence for every quote-author path and confirmation that QQBot config precedence matches other channels before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the QQBot extension’s ingress and configuration contract.
